text.title: Ios Signing And Provisioning Worked Examples
text.summary: One complete signing document for a client app on fastlane match with a token-key APNs setup and a 35-day rotation lead, with a note on every non-obvious value, and one bad document (agency-owned client app, certificates in the repo and in Slack, an Admin key on a laptop, TestFlight pointed at the sandbox host) showing what the validator and the reviewer reject.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: An agency builds "Northwind Field" for Northwind Ltd. Northwind owns the Apple Developer account (Team ID A1B2C3D4E5) and has invited the agency as App Manager. Signing assets are managed with fastlane match in an encrypted repository; GitHub Actions uploads TestFlight builds through an App Store Connect API key; the backend sends push through an APNs auth key. All certificates and profiles were created on 2026-02-14 and expire a year later.

example.title: Northwind Field signing document
example.note: `owning_team_id` is Northwind's, not the agency's, and the agency's role on that account is recorded; no transfer plan is needed because ownership was right from day one (r-client-account-owns-the-app).

Two certificates only: one shared distribution and one shared development identity, both in match; `readers` lists the CI identity and two people, which is the whole population that can sign (r-private-keys-in-secret-store-only).

The ASC key is App Manager (TestFlight upload needs it; Developer cannot), used by exactly one pipeline, and its `.p8` went into the GitHub secret at issue time because Apple never shows it again (r-asc-api-key-least-privilege).
Push uses a `.p8` auth key, so there is no APNs certificate and no APNs entry in the rotation calendar; the key does not expire (r-apns-token-key-over-cert).

TestFlight builds are signed for production APNs and the backend targets `api.push.apple.com` for them; only debug pairs with the sandbox host. This is the table that catches the BadDeviceToken failure before launch (r-push-environment-per-build-config).
Every rotation entry is 35 days ahead of the portal expiry with Maria named; `lead_days` is the number the reviewer checks against the rule's 30 (r-rotation-calendar-with-lead-time).

The runbook says which builds keep launching per certificate type (App Store builds survive a distribution revoke; development builds do not), is verified against Apple's own page, and the regeneration order starts with match so no per-developer identity is created in a panic (r-revocation-impact-documented).

example.title: What the validator and the reviewer reject
example.note: Validator output: `$.app: matches none of anyOf` (client app under the agency account with no transfer plan), `$.private_keys_outside_secret_store: must equal False, got True`, `$.certificates[0].per_developer_reason: missing required field`, `$.certificates[1].per_developer_reason: missing required field`, `$.asc_api_keys[0].role: 'Admin' not in enum ['Developer', 'App Manager']`, `$.asc_api_keys[0].p8_stored_at_issue: must equal True, got False`, `$.push.certificate_constraint: missing required field`, `$.push.certificate_expiry: missing required field`, `$.build_configs[0].apns_host: must equal 'api.push.apple.com', got 'api.sandbox.push.apple.com'`, `$.rotation_calendar[0].lead_days: 2 violates minimum=30`, `$.revocation_runbook.impact: 0 items, minItems=1`, `$.revocation_runbook.regeneration_order: 0 items, minItems=1`, `$.revocation_runbook.verified_against: 'https://someblog.example/ios-signing' does not match pattern '^https://developer\\.apple\\.com/'`, `$.review.binding_action_performed_by_agent: must equal False, got True`, `$.review.reviewer: missing required field`, `$.review.approved_on: missing required field`.

What the reviewer sees beyond the validator: `storage_location` values of "repo", "Slack thread" and "ask Maria" are not the secret store (r-private-keys-in-secret-store-only, r-inventory-every-signing-asset); the second distribution certificate has no rotation entry at all, and "someone on the team" is not a named person (r-rotation-calendar-with-lead-time); one Admin key shared with an analytics vendor means a vendor breach is full account control (r-asc-api-key-least-privilege).
